title: Health and nuisance pest management processes

lessons.title: Running health pest programmes at work
lessons.html:
Your workplace role

In this module you take part in managing real health and nuisance pest programmes: rodent and insect control at silo complexes and feed mills, fly control at dairies and piggeries, cockroach control in farm kitchens and workers' housing, bird proofing on warehouses, and audit-ready programmes for food factories and packhouses. You practise running service visits, analysing data and working with clients to fix the causes of pest problems.

A typical service visit

  1. Sign in and meet the client contact; review complaints and sightings.
  2. Service every monitoring device: bait stations, traps, insect light traps and sticky monitors; record results by device number.
  3. Inspect for new activity and conducive conditions.
  4. Apply targeted treatments where justified, following labels.
  5. Remove carcasses safely and replace damaged devices.
  6. Write the service report, including client actions.
  7. Brief the client and agree priorities.

Scenario: a dairy fly problem

A dairy farmer complains of heavy fly numbers in the milking parlour. You find wet manure and spilled feed around the calf pens, a blocked drain and an overflowing refuse bin. You recommend scraping and removing manure more often, fixing the drain, emptying and covering bins, and placing registered fly baits where the label allows away from milk and feed. You install a light trap in the dairy office area away from the milk room door. At the next visits, fly counts fall as sanitation improves. Most of the improvement came from removing breeding sites, not from chemicals.

lessons.title: Trends, audits and evidence
lessons.html:
Using data

Health pest programmes in food and feed businesses are audited. Practise turning device records into useful information.

  • Plot monthly activity per bait station or trap to find hot spots.
  • Compare light trap catches by insect type over time.
  • Mark activity on the site plan with colour codes.
  • Link trends to causes, such as a new door left open, construction, or a change in waste collection.

Preparing for an audit

DocumentCheck
Contract and scopeCurrent and signed
Site plan with device numbersUp to date
Service reportsComplete for every visit
Trend analysisDone at the agreed interval
Product labels and SDSsFor every product used
Operator registrations and trainingValid
Corrective actionsClosed out or with dates

Safety in sensitive sites

Never place loose rodenticide in food areas, protect food contact surfaces, keep bait stations secured, wear gloves for carcasses and droppings, and wash hands after each job.

Portfolio evidence

  • Service reports from visits you carried out.
  • Trend charts and site plans you prepared.
  • An audit file checklist you helped complete.
  • Mentor sign-offs and reflections.

Key points

  • Service every device, record by number and write a report with client actions on each visit.
  • Removing breeding sites and food sources often achieves more than chemicals.
  • Use trends and site plan hot spots to find causes.
  • Keep audit files complete: plan, reports, trends, labels, SDSs, registrations, corrective actions.
  • Follow strict safety rules in food and feed sites.
